subject: Request: Pinning ask for Nimbus Health (strata-13b variant) + canary plan
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Chen <sara.chen@nimbus.health>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Request: Pinning ask for Nimbus Health (strata-13b variant) + canary plan

Team —

Quick context: Nimbus (our largest upcoming healthcare pilot) is asking us to pin a specific serving variant of the new strata-13b model for their production traffic. Their compliance team requires a stable, versioned model for auditability and they will route regulated traffic to the pinned variant.

Why they want a pin:
- Determinism: they need a reproducible artifact for regulatory logs.
- Quality: their in-house eval showed small hallucination reduction on our candidate variant (strata-13b-v2-quant).
- Latency profile: median inference latency is slightly higher but within their SLA for deterministic output.

Attached I’m sharing the initial eval pack (nimbus_eval_results.csv) and telemetry snapshot (latency_telemetry_20261117.pdf). Quick summary of the numbers we care about:
- Candidate: strata-13b-v2-quant
- Median latency: +5% vs baseline (strata-13b-base)
- 95th pct latency: +9%
- Token cost: ~12% lower due to quant path
- Evals: slight improvement in factual QA and entity extraction on Nimbus testset (see CSV)

Asks:
1) Can Eng run a compatibility/kv-cache validation and confirm there are no unpredictability issues (tokenizer/vocab mapping, kv-cache size mismatches, attention kernel incompat)? We need a written compatibility acceptance to share with Nimbus.
2) Can Infra/Runtime propose a canary rollout plan that meets Nimbus’ need for a pinned, auditable model but minimizes blast radius? They want the pin in place by Dec 1 if possible.
3) Product: any gating concerns (pricing, routing policy, SLA notes) we should raise now?

Sara from Nimbus is cc’d — Sara, they can confirm here that they’re comfortable with a staged canary + monitoring approach and are prepared to accept a small latency delta in exchange for a stable pinned artifact.

I’m marking this as high priority for sales delivery. Rafael — can you keep procurement looped?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Pinning ask for Nimbus Health (strata-13b variant) + canary plan

Thanks for the write-up, Vanessa — quick technical follow-ups from Eng.

Short answer: pinning is plausible, but we need to validate a few compatibility vectors before we can approve a formal pin exception. My initial concerns:
- Tokenizer differences: does strata-13b-v2-quant use a different tokenizer or special token mapping compared to the baseline? If so, we need a delta map.
- KV-cache layout: quantized checkpoints sometimes change KV packing which can cause cache mismatches in multi-model routing scenarios. We need a KV parity test across sequence lengths (1, 128, 512).
- Model IO/schema: confirm there are no auxiliary outputs/hidden-state shape changes that downstream pipelines (reranker, streaming hooks) rely on.

What we need from Nimbus (or from the eval artifacts):
- Model manifest or hash of the checkpoint used for the eval (so we can match binary bits)
- Tokenization sample mapping for 20 representative prompts (we can diff against baseline)
- A short list of their production prompt prefixes/patterns (2-3 examples) so we can run the exact KV-cache verification.

Operationally, we can run an automated compatibility harness and return a report within 48 hours after we have their manifest + token samples. If the harness passes, Eng will prepare a short compatibility memo for the pin approval board.

Cc’ing Vivek to propose the canary parameters once Eng’s harness is green.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Request: Pinning ask for Nimbus Health (strata-13b variant) + canary plan

Thanks — from an infra/runtime POV I propose the following canary plan contingent on Eng's compatibility harness passing: 

Proposed canary (high level):
- Phase 1 (canary): 5% of Nimbus traffic -> strata-13b-v2-quant for 48 hours in us-east-1.
- Phase 2 (ramp): if no alerts, ramp to 25% for 72 hours and run secondary workload tests (batching behavior, KV-cache memory consumption).
- Full cutover only after both phases pass and Eng signoff.

Monitoring & rollback triggers (automated):
- Error rate (5xx or model inference errors) increase > 1.5% relative to baseline over a 30m window -> automatic rollback.
- p95 latency > 2x baseline for 15m -> automatic rollback.
- Quality degradation on the production prompt set (precision/recall drop > 3 pts) reported by shadow evaluation -> manual pause and investigation.

Operational notes:
- Fallback: route to baseline (strata-13b-base) immediately on rollback.
- KV-cache isolation: for the canary nodes we'll enable an isolated prefix store to avoid cache cross-contamination.
- Auditability: we will tag all inference traces with model_hash + pin_id and retain traces for 90 days for Nimbus audit (ask Legal/Compliance for retention exceptions if they require longer).

I created a short runbook stub in the Drive (canary_runbook.md) and opened INF-4732 so we can track infra changes and monitoring alerts.

If Eng can give compatibility go/no-go by EOD tomorrow I can schedule the canary for an early Dec window and align on rollout automation.

—Vivek
